reason: This passage from Nehemiah depicts Nehemiah, an appointed official, addressing the Hebrew people about Jerusalem's desolation and rallying them to rebuild the city walls. The people respond positively with 'Let us start building' (וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ נָק֣וּם וּבָנִ֔ינוּ). The only expressions of complaint and mockery come from external opponents—Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite servant, and Geshem the Arab—who jeer at and despise the rebuilding effort, not from the Hebrew people complaining about their own leaders.
